"GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PROJECT: APOCALYPSE SURVIVAL – MOBILE OPEN WORLD

Create a realistic, immersive, open-world zombie survival game for Android mobile devices, heavily inspired by the gameplay systems and atmosphere of DayZ.

The game must deliver a hardcore survival experience in a massive post-apocalyptic world where human survivors must explore, scavenge, build shelters, manage their physical condition, and survive against zombies and environmental dangers.

The experience should prioritize realism, freedom, exploration, tension, and player-driven gameplay.

1. GAME WORLD

Create a large, seamless open-world map featuring:

- Abandoned cities and towns.
- Small rural villages.
- Dense forests.
- Mountains and valleys.
- Rivers, lakes, and beaches.
- Farms and agricultural areas.
- Military bases.
- Hospitals and medical facilities.
- Police stations.
- Industrial complexes.
- Abandoned houses and supermarkets.
- Underground bunkers.
- Hunting locations.

The world should feel abandoned, dangerous, and realistic.

Implement a dynamic day and night cycle, realistic weather, fog, rain, thunderstorms, and changing environmental conditions.

2. PLAYER SYSTEM

Create realistic human survivor characters.

Include:

- First-person perspective.
- Third-person perspective.
- Character customization.
- Male and female characters.
- Clothing customization.
- Backpacks with different capacities.
- Character animations.
- Walking, running, crouching, jumping, and climbing.
- Realistic movement and stamina.
- Inventory management.

The player must be able to freely explore the world.

3. SURVIVAL MECHANICS

Implement a detailed survival system.

The player must manage:

- Hunger.
- Thirst.
- Body temperature.
- Energy.
- Stamina.
- Blood level.
- Health.
- Sleep and fatigue.
- Hydration.
- Infections and diseases.

Include different illnesses and environmental conditions.

Examples:

- Common cold.
- Fever.
- Food poisoning.
- Waterborne diseases.
- Wound infections.
- Hypothermia.
- Dehydration.
- Exhaustion.

Medical supplies should be valuable and necessary.

The player must search for food, clean water, medicine, clothing, and survival equipment.

4. ZOMBIE AI SYSTEM

Create intelligent zombie enemies.

Zombie behavior:

- Detect players through vision and sound.
- React to footsteps and gunshots.
- Patrol abandoned areas.
- Chase detected survivors.
- Search nearby locations.
- Attack when close.
- React to environmental disturbances.

Create different zombie variations:

- Normal infected.
- Fast infected.
- Strong infected.
- Armored infected.
- Special infected with unique behaviors.

Zombies should be dangerous, unpredictable, and challenging.

5. LOOT AND INVENTORY SYSTEM

Implement a realistic loot system.

Items should spawn in appropriate locations.

Examples:

- Food.
- Water bottles.
- Canned food.
- Medical supplies.
- Backpacks.
- Clothing.
- Tools.
- Flashlights.
- Batteries.
- Hunting equipment.
- Weapons.
- Ammunition.
- Building materials.

Implement:

- Item weight.
- Inventory capacity.
- Equipment slots.
- Item durability.
- Item condition.
- Clothing protection.
- Backpack storage.

Different locations should contain different types of loot.

6. BASE BUILDING SYSTEM

Allow players to construct their own bases anywhere in suitable areas of the map.

Building components:

- Wooden walls.
- Metal walls.
- Doors.
- Gates.
- Windows.
- Floors.
- Roofs.
- Watchtowers.
- Storage containers.
- Shelves.
- Campfires.
- Defensive structures.

Players must collect resources to build and maintain their bases.

Include:

- Base customization.
- Lockable doors.
- Storage systems.
- Building durability.
- Resource requirements.
- Protection against environmental conditions.

Bases should serve as safe locations where players can store equipment, food, medicine, and supplies.

7. WEAPONS AND EQUIPMENT

Implement a realistic equipment system with:

- Melee equipment.
- Firearms.
- Hunting equipment.
- Protective clothing.
- Helmets.
- Tactical vests.
- Backpacks.
- Medical equipment.

Include weapon condition, ammunition management, and realistic sound effects.

8. VEHICLE SYSTEM

Introduce usable vehicles:

- Cars.
- Pickup trucks.
- Motorcycles.
- Off-road vehicles.

Vehicles should require maintenance, fuel, and functional components.

Include vehicle inventory and storage.

9. WORLD INTERACTION

Allow players to interact with the environment.

Examples:

- Open doors.
- Search containers.
- Collect resources.
- Drink water.
- Eat food.
- Cook meals.
- Start campfires.
- Gather wood.
- Harvest plants.
- Hunt animals.
- Fish.
- Enter buildings.
- Search abandoned vehicles.

10. ANIMALS AND NATURE

Add wildlife:

- Deer.
- Wolves.
- Bears.
- Rabbits.
- Chickens.
- Cows.
- Boars.

Animals should have independent AI behaviors.

Include hunting, fishing, and food gathering.

11. AUDIO AND ATMOSPHERE

Create immersive environmental audio:

- Wind through trees.
- Rain.
- Thunder.
- Distant zombie sounds.
- Footsteps.
- Animal noises.
- Gunfire echo.
- Building sounds.
- Forest ambience.

Use realistic sound positioning to increase immersion.

12. MOBILE CONTROLS AND INTERFACE

Optimize the entire game for Android smartphones.

Include:

- Customizable touchscreen controls.
- Virtual joystick.
- Camera movement.
- Interaction buttons.
- Inventory interface.
- Health and survival indicators.
- Map interface.
- Equipment interface.
- Adjustable graphics settings.
- Performance optimization.

Support both first-person and third-person gameplay.

13. MULTIPLAYER FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

Build the initial version as a single-player open-world survival game.

However, organize the architecture to support future multiplayer implementation.

Future multiplayer features:

- Online servers.
- Human players sharing the same world.
- Player cooperation.
- Trading.
- Alliances.
- Base protection.
- Player-versus-player interactions.
- Persistent world progression.

Do not simulate multiplayer with AI characters and call it real multiplayer.

14. GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE

Use realistic 3D environments and atmospheric lighting.

Prioritize:

- Detailed environments.
- Realistic character models.
- High-quality textures.
- Natural animations.
- Dynamic lighting.
- Environmental effects.
- Optimized 3D assets.

Provide Low, Medium, High, and Ultra graphics presets.

The game must run smoothly on compatible Android devices, including mid-range smartphones.

Use level-of-detail systems, optimized textures, object culling, and efficient AI processing.

15. GAMEPLAY PHILOSOPHY

There should be no forced linear storyline.

The player must create their own survival story.

Every expedition should involve decisions, risks, and rewards.

The world should feel dangerous even when no zombies are visible.

Resources must be valuable, exploration must be meaningful, and survival must require planning.

16. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Develop the game in stages.

STAGE 1:

- Playable 3D character.
- First-person and third-person cameras.
- Basic movement.
- Small open-world map.
- Basic zombie AI.

STAGE 2:

- Loot spawning.
- Inventory.
- Hunger and thirst.
- Health and stamina.
- Basic diseases.

STAGE 3:

- Weapons and equipment.
- Medical system.
- Weather.
- Day and night cycle.

STAGE 4:

- Base building.
- Resource gathering.
- Storage.
- Crafting.

STAGE 5:

- Vehicles.
- Animals.
- Expanded map.
- Advanced AI.

STAGE 6:

- Multiplayer-ready architecture.
- Online server development.
- Persistent multiplayer world.

IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION:

Do not attempt to create every feature simultaneously.

Build a functional and playable prototype first. Implement and test each system independently before expanding the game.

If a feature is too complex for the current mobile game development environment, implement a simplified functional version while preserving the intended gameplay experience.

FINAL OBJECTIVE:

Create a true mobile hardcore survival experience inspired by DayZ, featuring a massive open world, realistic human survivors, dangerous zombies, deep survival mechanics, diseases, exploration, crafting, base building, vehicles, and future multiplayer support.

The final result should feel like a complete post-apocalyptic survival sandbox, not a simple zombie shooting game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile zombie-survival game prototype in the existing project, following the staged-development approach in the prompt.
- Create a functional first playable version now; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Requirements
- Single-player open-world survival prototype, mobile-friendly with touchscreen controls.
- Start with a playable character, first-/third-person cameras where feasible, movement, a small world, and basic zombie AI; implement later systems as practical.
- Aim for immersive survival gameplay and a polished interface; multiplayer is future architecture only, not simulated.
- Verify the game and report assumptions briefly when finishing.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a static HTML/CSS/Canvas 2D game because the repository had no existing game framework or code.
- Prototype uses top-down gameplay, procedural 2D terrain, and a compact explorable county rather than attempting a full 3D open world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with game HUD, start screen, inventory/map modals, mobile controls, and survival indicators.
- Created `style.css` with responsive styling and mobile layout/touch controls.
- Began `game.js` with player/zombie/loot systems, terrain rendering, and interaction/UI logic.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`; the latest write currently ends after `drawWorld()` and does not yet include update loop, input handlers, modals, or the closing IIFE.
- Run `node --check game.js`, fix syntax/runtime errors, start the static game, and verify via browser capture.
- Add a simple start/controls explanation if needed, then summarize delivered features and prototype limitations.

### Blocked
- `game.js` is incomplete; current file is not yet a playable complete implementation.

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` from the present `drawWorld()` definition, implementing survival updates, zombie behavior, UI/modal and touch/keyboard input, and closing the script wrapper.
2. Run `node --check game.js`; correct issues and confirm all referenced functions/elements exist.
3. Launch with the project’s static start workflow and inspect gameplay on desktop and mobile; fix visual or interaction defects.
4. Provide a concise completion note explaining the top-down 2D prototype assumption and major playable systems.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main game page and all UI structure.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: In-progress Canvas game logic; continue implementation here.
- `start.sh`: Project start launcher.

## Important Context
- Earlier `node --check game.js` failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'`; the file was then replaced and extended, but no syntax check has been run since.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile zombie-survival prototype in the existing project.
- Deliver a functional first playable version and briefly report assumptions and limitations.

## Requirements
- Single-player open-world survival prototype with touchscreen-friendly controls.
- Include movement, a small world, basic zombie AI, survival gameplay, and a polished interface.
- Multiplayer is future architecture only, not simulated.

## Decisions
- Use static HTML/CSS/Canvas 2D because the repository had no existing game framework.
- Use top-down gameplay with procedural terrain and a compact explorable county instead of full 3D.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game page, responsive HUD, start/death screens, inventory/map/pause modals, and mobile controls.
- Implemented player movement, building collision, zombies and combat, loot gathering, consumable supplies, survival meters, weather/day cycle, and map.
- `node --check game.js` passes; served the page locally and captured desktop and mobile screenshots.

### Active
- Test interactive gameplay in-browser, check console/runtime behavior, and fix any issues found.
- Finish with a concise feature and limitation summary.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run an interactive browser test of starting, movement, combat, interaction, inventory, map, pause, and mobile controls.
2. Fix any runtime or gameplay defects; rerun `node --check game.js`.
3. Summarize the delivered prototype and its top-down 2D scope.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Canvas rendering, game state, gameplay systems, and input handling.
- `index.html`: Game interface and modal/control structure.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start launcher.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Local static server was started with `python3 -m http.server 8765`; desktop and mobile screenshots are in `/tmp/opencode/afterlight.png` and `/tmp/opencode/afterlight-mobile.png`.
- The screenshots verified page rendering only; interactive gameplay has not yet been tested.

PROJECT: APOCALYPSE SURVIVAL – MOBILE OPEN WORLD

Create a realistic, immersive, open-world zombie survival game for Android mobile devices, heavily inspired by the gameplay systems and atmosphere of DayZ.

The experience should prioritize realism, freedom, exploration, tension, and player-driven gameplay.

1. GAME WORLD

- Abandoned cities and towns.
- Small rural villages.
- Dense forests.
- Mountains and valleys.

- Farms and agricultural areas.
- Military bases.
- Hospitals and medical facilities.
- Police stations.
- Industrial complexes.
- Abandoned houses and supermarkets.
- Underground bunkers.
- Hunting locations.

The world should feel abandoned, dangerous, and realistic.

Implement a dynamic day and night cycle, realistic weather, fog, rain, thunderstorms, and changing environmental conditions.

2. PLAYER SYSTEM

Create realistic human survivor characters.

Include:

- First-person perspective.
- Third-person perspective.
- Character customization.
- Male and female characters.
- Clothing customization.
- Backpacks with different capacities.
- Character animations.
- Walking, running, crouching, jumping, and climbing.
- Realistic movement and stamina.
- Inventory management.

The player must be able to freely explore the world.

3. SURVIVAL MECHANICS

Implement a detailed survival system.

The player must manage:

- Hunger.
- Thirst.
- Body temperature.
- Energy.
- Stamina.
- Blood level.
- Health.
- Sleep and fatigue.
- Hydration.
- Infections and diseases.

Include different illnesses and environmental conditions.

Examples:

- Common cold.
- Fever.
- Food poisoning.
- Waterborne diseases.
- Wound infections.
- Hypothermia.
- Dehydration.
- Exhaustion.

Medical supplies should be valuable and necessary.

The player must search for food, clean water, medicine, clothing, and survival equipment.

4. ZOMBIE AI SYSTEM

Create intelligent zombie enemies.

Zombie behavior:

- Detect players through vision and sound.
- React to footsteps and gunshots.
- Patrol abandoned areas.
- Chase detected survivors.
- Search nearby locations.
- Attack when close.
- React to environmental disturbances.

Create different zombie variations:

- Normal infected.
- Fast infected.
- Strong infected.
- Armored infected.
- Special infected with unique behaviors.

Zombies should be dangerous, unpredictable, and challenging.

5. LOOT AND INVENTORY SYSTEM

Items should spawn in appropriate locations.

Examples:

- Food.
- Water bottles.
- Canned food.
- Medical supplies.
- Backpacks.
- Clothing.
- Tools.
- Flashlights.

- Item condition.
- Clothing protection.

6. BASE BUILDING SYSTEM

Allow players to construct their own bases anywhere in suitable areas of the map.

- Wooden walls.
- Metal walls.
- Doors.
- Gates.
- Windows.
- Floors.
- Roofs.
- Watchtowers.

- Defensive structures.

- Base customization.

```js
let daylight; // 0 night, 1 noon
if(clock>=7 && clock<=17) daylight=1;

else if(clock>=20||clock<4.5) daylight=0;

darkness=(1-daylight)*.55;
```
